This is the intended sequential handoff, not a live concurrent edit, so I proceeded rather than blocking on a completed parent (blocking would deadlock the chain).

The fix cut markup-leading SOP/LOP summaries from 27 to 17 over 1571 indexed pages. All covered classes reached 0; the residual 17 are line-level or heading-level markup that the paragraph rule cannot address without a different rule.

for_ruling.detail: The deprecation description begins with an inline ':warning:' admonition token glued to real prose (e.g. ':warning:Deprecated: The Cloud SOP is now deprecated.'). The paragraph is genuinely prose, so the markup-only paragraph rule must NOT drop it. Proposed follow-up (a distinct LINE-level rule): strip a leading inline ':name:' admonition token from the chosen summary. Deliberately not done here to keep the diff to the paragraph rule.

for_ruling.item: '= Heading =' stub/redirect pages (7 incl. one BOM variant: nodes/sop/lopimport '= LOP Import =', nodes/sop/name 'U+FEFF= Name =', ...)
for_ruling.detail: These pages carry only a wiki heading and no prose paragraph, so the honest answer is UNKNOWN, but the existing title-drop heuristic cannot fire (it needs a following paragraph). Proposed follow-up: treat a lone '= Heading =' paragraph as a droppable title so the page reports the honest unknown (rule 6). Not a '#'/':name...:' directive, so out of the paragraph rule as scoped.

These are category index pages, not node types. An Identify lookup keys on a node's operator help URL (derive_help_keys) and never resolves to '/index', so this does not affect the feature. Proposed: no product fix needed; optionally exclude '/index' pages from any future corpus audit.
